examples.en: Is this answer right?

examples.ko: 네, 맞아요. 그 사람이 제 언니예요.
examples.en: Yes, that's right. That person is my older sister.
My friend is right. I was wrong.

examples.ko: 시험 문제를 열 개 다 맞았어요.
examples.en: I got all ten exam questions right.

examples.ko: 이 문장 맞아요? 한번 봐 주세요.
examples.en: Is this sentence correct? Please take a look.

explain: ‘맞다’는 ‘맞는 답’뿐 아니라 ‘몸에 맞는 옷’처럼 딱 어울린다는 뜻으로도 써요.

explain_en: 맞다 is not only ‘correct’. It also means ‘fits’, as in 몸에 맞는 옷 (clothes that fit your body).

en: to be wrong; to be incorrect

examples.en: My answer was wrong.
I got two questions wrong on the test.
The particle in this sentence is wrong.
It's okay to make mistakes. Let's go slowly.
The bill is wrong. Please check it again.

explain: ‘틀리다’는 ‘맞지 않다(wrong)’이고, ‘다르다’는 ‘같지 않다(different)’예요. 한국 사람도 가끔 헷갈려요.

explain_en: 틀리다 means wrong; 다르다 means different. Korean people sometimes mix them up too.

examples.en: The text on the screen is too small.

examples.ko: 카드에 제 이름이 한 글자 틀렸어요.
examples.en: My name on the card has one letter wrong.
How do you read this letter?
The letters on the sign are very big.
I can't see small letters well.

explain: ‘글자’는 한 글자 한 글자를 말하고, ‘글씨’는 손으로 쓴 글자 모양이에요. ‘글씨가 예뻐요’처럼 써요.

dict_examples.en: The handwriting is sloppy, so I can't tell whether this letter is '서' or '저'.

explain_en: 글자 is each single letter or character. 글씨 is how handwriting looks, as in 글씨가 예뻐요 (your handwriting is nice).

examples.ko: 전화로 친구 목소리가 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: I can't hear my friend's voice well on the phone.
My voice doesn't come out well in the morning.
The radio announcer's voice is really nice.
In the library, I talk in a quiet voice.
My voice is similar to my mom's.

explain_en: 목소리 joins 목 (throat) and 소리 (sound). Say 크다/작다 for loudness and 좋다/예쁘다 for how it sounds.

examples.en: Please explain this word in detail.
I studied the map closely before the trip.
I read the email carefully. The date was wrong.
Read the contract carefully. Check your name too.

examples.ko: 그 일은 자세히 몰라요. 제 친구한테 물어보세요.
examples.en: I don't know the details of that. Please ask my friend.

explain: ‘자세히’는 끝이 ‘히’예요 (자세이 ✕). 형용사는 ‘자세하다’이고, 명사 앞에서는 ‘자세한 설명’처럼 말해요.

explain_en: Spell it 자세히, ending in 히. The adjective is 자세하다; before a noun it becomes 자세한, as in 자세한 설명.

examples.en: Copy the words on the board into your notebook exactly as they are.
I'll have the same, please.
My younger brother looks exactly like Dad.

examples.ko: 저를 보고 똑같이 따라 해 보세요.
examples.en: Watch me and copy exactly what I do.

examples.ko: 김밥 한 줄을 친구하고 똑같이 나눠요.
examples.en: I split one roll of gimbap equally with my friend.

explain: ‘같이’는 ‘함께(together)’이고 ‘똑같이’는 ‘완전히 같게(exactly the same)’예요. 소리가 비슷하지만 뜻이 달라요.

explain_en: 같이 means together; 똑같이 means exactly the same way. They sound alike but mean different things.

en: to be exact; to be accurate

examples.en: The time in the note is correct.
This map app is really accurate.
Please tell me the exact address.

examples.ko: 일기 예보가 정확했어요. 정말 비가 왔어요.
examples.en: The weather forecast was accurate. It really rained.
The bus times aren't accurate.

explain_en: Use it for time, numbers and information that have no mistakes. 확실하다 is different: it means you are certain.

examples.en: I talked a lot with my friend over the weekend.
Is that story true?
What's it about? I want to hear it too.

examples.ko: 저녁마다 아이한테 옛날 얘기를 해 줘요.
examples.en: Every evening I tell my child an old story.

examples.ko: 집에서는 회사 얘기를 하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to talk about work at home.

explain_en: 얘기 is short for 이야기. People say it often when talking. In writing, 이야기 is more common.

p.n: 대담 is a formal, staged conversation, so it is odd for a casual chat with a friend.
